Q: Android application Google/Firebase login integration not working A:

For me, the account picker was not opening, and yours is, so the following may or may not solve your issue.

If you go to the app signing page, you will see two keys: classical key and post quantum key. But there is also an option to download certificates just below these key sections.

If you see that downloaded folder, there is a third certificate called deployment-cert, which also has a pair of SHA1/SHA256 that need to go in Firebase and services.json, etc.

I found this out by connecting my Android app in developer mode and checking what SHA it is sending to the Google servers. This showed that there is a whole different key. From there, I found the download certifications, which confirmed the third key.

Q: Teradata JDBC Error 1338 after certain number of batch executions A:

So few notes here.

  1. The first is GC. It's not an issue in the usual java program but under a load of millions records try to do eventually Thread.sleep with single seconds. This will trigger GC. I found some race conditions in the Teradata JDBC driver ver 17.00.00.03. For performance purpose it is reusing old objects with a weak reference to something to be collected. When working with fastload™ or multiload™ loads, this became crucial.
  2. Ensure you have enough space in your database. This also causes this exception.

Q: Is there a simple way to convert setup.py to pyproject.toml A:

While dealing with some pyproject.toml issues, I encountered this project:

https://pypi.org/project/ini2toml/

The projects description:

This project is experimental and under active development Issue reports and contributions are very welcome. The original purpose of this project is to help migrating setup.cfg files to PEP 621, but by extension it can also be used to convert any compatible .ini/.cfg file to .toml.

While this only helps to turn .cfg/.ini files to PEP 621 .toml, there is another project that turn setup.py files into cfg files.

https://github.com/gvalkov/setuptools-py2cfg

This script helps convert existing setup.py files to setup.cfg in the format expected by setuptools.

Combining these two processes could potentially come up with an automated way to transform the files:

pip install ini2toml setuptools-py2cfg
ini2toml <(setuptools-py2cfg) > pyproject.toml

Q: Write multiple values to file in mounted local folder A:

I saw your code in main.py in link but you should show it directly in question.

Problem is that you assign value to variable saR/saRL in loop - and in every loop it has different value. And after loop it has only last value.

If you print it in loop then you finally see all values in browser
but after loop you have only last value in variable so it writes only last filename in file.

You may have to write it also in loop

   with open("/local/small.txt", "w") as f:

        for index, row in df.iterrows():
            # dxf_text = row['attributes.SaR_Grid_Maps']
            saR = row['attributes.SaR_Grid_Maps']
            saRL = row['attributes.SaRL_Grid_Maps']
            print(f'{saR}\n{saRL}') #print to console in a Chromium browser

            # ... inside loop ...

            f.write(f'{saR}\n' )

but this makes problem with mounting and unmounting.
It would need to create one loop for small.txt and another for large.txt

But you can create list with all filenames
and later use another loop to write them

all_saR = []
all_saRL = []

for index, row in df.iterrows():
    # dxf_text = row['attributes.SaR_Grid_Maps']
    saR = row['attributes.SaR_Grid_Maps']
    saRL = row['attributes.SaRL_Grid_Maps']
    print(f'{saR}\n{saRL}') #print to console in a Chromium browser

    # ... inside loop ...

    all_saR.append( saR )
    all_saRL.append( saRL )

# ... later ...

with open("/local/small.txt", "w") as f:
    for saR in all_saR:
        f.write(f'{saR}\n' )

# ... later ...

with open("/local/large.txt", "w") as f:
    for saRL in all_saRL:
        f.write(f'{saRL}\n' )

Eventually you may convert list to one string and write it all at once

# ... later ...

text = "\n".join(all_saR)

with open("/local/small.txt", "w") as f:
     f.write(text)

# ... later ...

text = "\n".join(all_saRL)

with open("/local/large.txt", "w") as f:
     f.write(text)

If you don't need to display values then you could reduce your loop to two lines:

all_saR = df['attributes.SaR_Grid_Maps'].to_list()
all_saRL = df['attributes.SaRL_Grid_Maps'].to_list()

Eventually later you could use loop to display values from lists as pairs:

for saR, saRL in zip(all_saR, all_saRL):
    print(f'{saR}\n{saRL}')
